title: Rename each PIM Manager job to its standard name
purpose: Renames each PIM Manager job of one install to its standard name caj-pim-<purpose> by creating the new job with the same spec, proving it, switching to it and disabling the old job -- the old job is deleted only with -DeleteOld, after the proof and the switch.
whenToRun: Once per install for the naming standard (jobs named caj-pim-<purpose>), after the identity move (every job runs as its own id-pim-<role>). First without -Apply (the plan, read-only, for the approval), then -Apply -Role <role> one role at a time. A role that reports 'waiting' (its old job was running) is finished by running the same command again.

runAs.name: Contributor + User Access Administrator
runAs.why: Creates the new job, reads the old job's secrets (listSecrets) to copy them, copies the job-scoped role assignments to the new job, starts the proof run, switches the settings and sets the old job's trigger to Manual.

runAs.name: The Invardia Support app's audited SQL access (Invoke-InvardiaSupportSql) to the PIM database
runAs.why: Switches pim.Settings 'SchedulerTickJobId' and 'InstallNames' to the new job.

runAs.name: Log Analytics Reader
runAs.scope: the Log Analytics workspace of the install's Container Apps environment (only with -SqlViaJob)
runAs.why: Reads the one-time job's result line (its console log) when the database is private and pim.Settings is reached through that job.

changes.object: the new job caj-pim-<purpose>: the old job's spec (image, command, variables, resources, registries, secrets, identity id-pim-<role>, environment, workload profile, timeouts), trigger Manual until the switch, tagged pim-renamed-from=<old job>
changes.why: Azure cannot rename a job; the standard name needs a new one.
changes.undo: Delete the NEW job only (the command is in the run record); the old job is untouched until the switch.

changes.object: each role assignment made on the old job itself (for example the Manager's Container Apps Jobs Operator on the engine job, a job's Reader on itself), given on the new job
changes.permission: the same Azure role for the same principal
changes.why: The same rights on the new job before anything switches; nothing is removed from the old job.
changes.undo: Kept: harmless on the new job; no role assignment is ever deleted by this script.

changes.object: one run of the new job for the proof
changes.why: Proves the new job works before anything switches; a failed proof switches nothing.
changes.undo: Nothing to undo: a normal run.

changes.object: the new job gets the old job's schedule (same cron); every variable of the Manager app and of the other jobs that names the old job (PIM_TickJobId, PIM_TickJobName, PIM_ENGINE_JOB_NAME, PIM_UpdateJobName, PIM_JobId, ...) names the new one
changes.scope: the PIM apps and jobs of the resource group
changes.why: Everything that starts, reads or records the job uses the new one.
changes.undo: The reverse switch per app / job (the command is in the run record).

changes.why: The Manager and every reader find the job by its new name.
changes.undo: The previous value is in the run record with the command that writes it back.

changes.object: the OLD job's trigger set to Manual (its schedule off); the job, its identity and its rights are kept
changes.why: The old job no longer runs.
changes.undo: Set the old job's trigger back to its schedule (the command is in the run record).

changes.object: ONLY with -DeleteOld, after the proof and the switch read back: the OLD job (its system-assigned identity goes with it); its full spec and job-scoped role assignments are written to the rollback record first, then the delete is read back (404)
changes.why: Owner decision 2026-11-09: the renamed install keeps no old job.
changes.undo: Re-create the job from the rollback record (PUT with the recorded spec and trigger, then its role assignments); secret values are re-entered, and a re-created job has a new system identity.

changes.object: ONLY with -DeleteOld: old id-pim-* user-assigned identities that no container app, job, SQL server or storage account attaches any more and that are not a standard id-pim-<role> (re-checked at delete time; an attached identity is never deleted); each recorded first (name, client id, principal id, role assignments), read back 404
changes.why: No unused old identity left behind; its role assignments are not deleted.
changes.undo: Re-create the identity from the record (it gets a new principal: grant its recorded roles to it).

changes.object: ONLY with -SqlViaJob (a private database): a one-time job caj-pim-renamesql in the install's own environment, with the identity, image and image-pull identity of the install's database job (caj-pim-dbinit, else ca-pim-dbinit), tagged pim-one-time-job=job-rename-sql; started once per read or write of pim.Settings, then removed and read back gone -- also after a failed step. No identity gets a new right
changes.why: A private database cannot be reached from outside; the job reaches it over the install's own network, as its database job does.
changes.undo: Nothing to undo: the job is removed at the end of each run. A job a killed run left behind carries the tag and is removed by the next run (or delete caj-pim-renamesql in the Azure portal).

parameters.name: SubscriptionId
parameters.help: The subscription of the PIM install.

parameters.name: ResourceGroup
parameters.help: The resource group of the PIM install.

parameters.name: Apply
parameters.help: Rename the role in -Role. Without it the script only plans.

parameters.name: Role
parameters.help: The ONE role to rename with -Apply: engine, updater, dbinit, publish, downlink, docs.

parameters.name: LogDir
parameters.help: Where the plan, the plan text and the per-role record are written.

parameters.name: DeleteOld
parameters.help: After the proof and the switch read back, delete the old job and the old id-pim-* identities nothing attaches any more (rollback record first, 404 read back). Without it the old job is disabled and kept.

parameters.name: SqlDatabase
parameters.default: PIM_SqlDatabase of the Manager app, else PimPlatform

parameters.name: SqlViaJob
parameters.help: For an install whose database is private: read and write pim.Settings through a one-time job inside the install's network (the database job's identity), created, run once and removed each time; the result is read from its log lines. -WhatIf creates no job.

readsOnly: the container apps and jobs of the resource group (their spec, identity, trigger and variables)
the role assignments made on each job (atScope)
the executions of each job (a running one is waited for, never stopped)
network: api.loganalytics.io (only with -SqlViaJob: the one-time job's result lines)
whatIf: Without -Apply the script is read-only either way. With -Apply -WhatIf it reads everything, prints the plan and, for the role, one line for each step it would take (create, copy, prove, switch, disable) -- nothing is written.
undo: Every run writes a record to -LogDir with each change in order and its exact undo command; a failed run prints them newest first. Without -DeleteOld nothing is deleted (the old job is kept, Manual); with it every delete is recorded before it happens. A failed proof leaves the old job untouched.
